basics.q: How many pillars does Islam have?
basics.why: The testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan and Hajj (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim).

basics.q: How many obligatory rak’ahs does the Fajr prayer have?
basics.why: Fajr is two rak’ahs; Maghrib three; Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

basics.q: How many obligatory rak’ahs does Maghrib have?
basics.why: Maghrib is the three-rak’ah prayer.

basics.q: Which surah was the first to be revealed, in its opening verses?
basics.why: “Read in the name of your Lord who created” (96:1) began the revelation in the cave of Hira.

basics.q: Which is the longest surah of the Qur’an?
basics.why: Al-Baqarah has 286 verses.

basics.q: Which is the shortest surah?
basics.why: Al-Kawthar has three short verses.

basics.q: Which surah has no “Bismillah” at its beginning?
basics.why: Surah At-Tawbah (9) is the one surah that does not begin with it.

basics.q: Which surah contains the Bismillah twice?
basics.why: An-Naml 27:30 quotes the letter of Sulayman, which begins with it.

basics.q: In which month is fasting obligatory?
basics.why: Ramadan, the ninth month (2:185).

basics.q: In which surah is Laylat al-Qadr named?
basics.why: Surah Al-Qadr (97): “better than a thousand months”.

basics.q: Who was the first mu’adhdhin of Islam?
basics.why: Bilal, the Prophet’s mu’adhdhin in Madinah.

basics.q: In which cave did the Prophet ﷺ receive the first revelation?
basics.why: He used to retire to the cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur.

basics.q: Which prophet built the Ka‘bah with his son Isma‘il?
basics.why: “And when Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House with Isma‘il” (2:127).

basics.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
basics.why: He called out in the darkness: “There is no god but You, glory be to You” (21:87).

basics.q: To which prophet was the Torah (Tawrah) given?
basics.why: Musa, the Zabur to Dawud and the Injil to ‘Isa.

basics.q: Which angel brought the revelation to the prophets?
basics.why: Jibril (Gabriel).

basics.q: Which Companion was given the title “Sword of Allah”?
basics.why: The Prophet ﷺ called Khalid “a sword among the swords of Allah” (Sahih al-Bukhari).

basics.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ?
basics.why: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the first to believe in him.

basics.q: Who was the first caliph after the Prophet ﷺ?
basics.why: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq.

basics.q: Which Companion is known as al-Faruq?
basics.why: “The one who distinguishes truth from falsehood”.

basics.q: In which city did the Prophet ﷺ spend the last ten years of his life?
basics.why: After the Hijrah in the year 622 CE.

basics.q: Which battle took place in the second year after the Hijrah?
basics.why: Badr, in Ramadan of 2 AH.

basics.q: Towards what direction do Muslims pray?
basics.why: The qibla was changed from Jerusalem to the Ka‘bah (2:144).

basics.q: What is the Qur’an’s opening surah called?
basics.why: Al-Fatiha, “The Opening”, with seven verses.

basics.q: How many verses does Surah Al-Fatiha have?
basics.why: It is “the seven oft-repeated verses” (15:87).

basics.q: What is zakat al-fitr given at the end of?
basics.why: It is given before the Eid prayer, to purify the fast and feed the poor.

basics.q: Which prophet is known as Khalilullah, the close friend of Allah?
basics.why: Allah “took Ibrahim as a close friend” (4:125).

basics.q: What is the Arabic word for the pilgrimage to Makkah?
basics.why: Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah; Umrah can be performed at any time.

basics.q: What does “Islam” mean at its root?
basics.why: From the root s-l-m: submission to Allah, and peace.

basics.q: Which surah is recommended to be read on Friday?
basics.why: Whoever reads Surah al-Kahf on Friday will have a light between the two Fridays (as reported by al-Hakim and others).
